newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM chairs first cross-party council.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM chairs first cross-party council.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin chaired the first meeting of a new cross-party Consultative Council on Thursday and said he was certain that a common approach could solve Russia's biggest problems.

It appeared from television film that some party leaders, including communist chief Gennady Zyuganov, had preferred not to attend. The communists were represented by Gennady Seleznyov, chairman of the State Duma lower house of parliament.

Officials said the political crisis in Belarus and the peace process in Chechnya were at the top of the agenda for the meeting, which Chernomyrdin chaired in the absence of President Boris Yeltsin, who is convalescing from heart surgery.
Yeltsin set up the body on October 21.
Its permanent members are himself, Chernomyrdin and the speakers of the two chambers of parliament.
It aims to promote greater coordination in policy between the presidential administration, the government and parliament, where opposition communists dominate the Duma.
Television film showed Chernomyrdin meeting Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, who was standing in for Yeltsin, Seleznyov and Yegor Stroyev, chairman of the Federation Council upper house.

Others present included Ivan Rybkin, secretary of the Kremlin Security Council and chief negotiator in Chechnya, Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov and Sergei Belyayev, parliamentary leader of Chernomyrdin's Our Home is Russia party.

Zyuganov was reported to have said he would not attend in the presence of Chubais, whom communists accuse of usurping power during Yeltsin's prolonged absence. But he was content that Seleznyov, a communist, should be at the meeting.
The Duma speaker had previously refused to take part in the council because of Chubais's participation.
